title: Token-aware admission control and progressive model-paths for OOM avoidance
creator: Aisha Thompson
description: Design and implement a token-aware admission controller plus progressive model-path execution to avoid GPU OOMs during spikes and long-context requests. This ticket covers request scoring, per-request KV budget estimation, fast-path quantized execution, graceful token-shedding heuristics, CPU spill fallback with latency guards, and an observable retry/backoff policy. The goal is predictable tail latency and nearly-zero customer-visible failures for long-context and large-batch workloads.
rationale: We continue to see OOMs for requests with atypical sequence lengths or sudden batch coalescing. Existing eviction-first strategies cause unpredictable latencies and recovered requests often fail with 5xx. A proactive, admission-first approach that binds per-request budgets and degrades work onto cheaper execution paths will reduce OOMs and improve SLO compliance.
design_decisions: Introduce a lightweight admission score computed from (expected_output_tokens, prefix_kv_size_estimate, batching_penalty) produced by the API ingress layer.
Reserve a per-GPU soft KV budget and an emergency spill budget; admission rejects or reroutes requests that cannot be served without breaching soft budget.
Add progressive model-paths: full precision runtime -> int8 fast-path -> quantized faster model variant -> CPU-exec fallback. Each path has a defined memory and latency envelope.
Implement per-request KV trimming policies: prefix-only trimming, drop non-essential cached past tokens, and preferential retention for hot prefixes defined by recent hit-rate.
Retry policy: exponential backoff with randomized jitter; on admission fail, the router attempts a lower-memory model-path with a conservative backoff to avoid stampeding.
Make admission scoring adaptive via an online estimator trained on recent sequence length distributions and successful path decisions.
Expose metrics for admission pass/fail, chosen model-path, memory headroom, and customer-visible retries for observability and alerting.
Keep default behavior backward compatible: only opt-in progressive quantized-paths per deployment or by model tag.
Safety: do not allow quantized fast-path for models or customers that have disabled lossy execution; honor customer isolation / policy.
Fallback to dedicated pool routing for high-value customers if admission fails on shared pool and dedicated pool has capacity.
Record admission decision rationale in request trace for postmortem and ML-driven tuning.
acceptance_criteria: New admission controller returns decision for every incoming request and logs decision metadata to tracing with <100us median overhead.
Per-GPU soft KV budget enforced; no silent breach—if attempted, the request is denied or rerouted with a clear error code and retry hint.
Progressive model-paths implemented end-to-end and annotated in telemetry (full, int8-fast, quant-variant, cpu-fallback).
System-level OOMs related to long-context requests reduced by >= 80% on canary cluster under synthetic tail-heavy traffic compared to baseline.
SLOs: 99th percentile request success (no 5xx due to OOM) improves by >=50% for mixed-length workloads on canary.
Automated e2e tests that simulate batch coalescing and very long prefixes validate token-shedding and retry behaviour without violating correctness regression thresholds for opted-in models.
Runbook updated with new error codes and operator steps for admission/retry incidents.
tasks: API ingress: compute admission score and attach to request header (ENG change)
Runtime: implement per-GPU soft KV budget enforcement and model-path selector
Runtime: implement fast int8 execution path switch with controlled precision policy
Routing: implement reroute to dedicated pools and model-variant resolution
KV cache: add prefix-priority tags and trimming operations exposed to runtime
Observability: add metrics and traces (admission_decision, selected_path, kv_headroom, retry_count)
E2E: add synthetic test harness for long-context bursts and batch coalescing
Docs/runbook: draft operator runbook for new admission fail modes and retry guidance
Security/Settings: add customer opt-out flag for lossy execution paths
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable admission scoring in canary cluster with logging only (no enforced denies) for 3 days to collect calibration data
Phase 2 (sized canary): Enforce soft KV budget with reroute-to-quantized-path enabled for non-sensitive models; monitor OOM and latency delta for 1 week
Phase 3 (progressive): Enable int8-fast path and CPU-fallback for a subset of customers; keep opt-out respected
Phase 4 (global): Gradual rollout across regions with playbook; provide opt-in flags for early customers and dedicated-pool auto-fallback for enterprise tenants
Rollback: revert to logging-only admission and allow runtime to resume eviction-first behavior
test_plan: Unit: admission score correctness and scoring edge-cases
Integration: end-to-end routing across model-paths with synthetic long prefixes
Load: stress test with 2x normal tail-length distribution and batch coalescing to measure OOM rate
Chaos: kill GPU processes during admission to ensure controller correctly reroutes and records failures
Regression: compare model outputs between full-precision and int8-fast for opted-in models and ensure quality delta within allowed thresholds
